saket kumar New Delhi, 4 November The Union Cabinet on Wed- nesday approved a ₹2,814- crore support scheme to establish domestic critical mineral processing plants for lithium and nickel, a move wel- comed by industry players who said it would address a key gap in India’s critical mineral value chain and help reduce dependence on imports. Under the scheme, which will run from FY27 to FY31, the government will provide a capital subsidy of 30 per cent for setting up two lithium processing plants and two nickel processing plants. The plants will have minimum pro- cessing capacities of 30,000 tonnes each for lithium and 50,000 tonnes each for nickel. The maximum capital sup- port has been capped at ₹500 crore per beneﬁciary for lithium plants and ₹900 crore for nickel plants. The scheme aims to develop domestic pro- cessing capabilities for con- verting lithium and nickel ores and intermediate products into high-purity compounds. Cobalt is also expected to be recovered as a by-product of nickel processing. Beneﬁciaries will be selected in a two-stage pro- cess, beginning with technical qualiﬁcation, followed by ﬁnancial bidding. For each mineral, two beneﬁciaries will be selected based on the least- cost criterion, with preference given to bidders seeking the lowest capital expenditure support from the government. The incentives will be dis- bursed in three tranches linked to the achievement of speciﬁed milestones. Domestic beneﬁciation and processing infrastructure remains at a nascent stage, with commercial-scale pro- jects facing challenges such as high capital requirements, limited availability of suitable technologies and constrained access to raw materials. Attero co-founder and CEO Nitin Gupta said the scheme addressed a key gap in India's critical mineral value chain — domestic processing capacity. While the country was taking steps to secure access to critical min- eral resources, developing the ability to process them into high-purity materials was equally important to reduce import dependence and strengthen supply chain security, he said. LOHUM founder and CEO Rajat Verma said the scheme could help India move from importing towards developing domestic supplies by suppor- ting facilities that convert lithium and nickel into high- purity compounds. ₹2K cr push for lithium, nickel processing plants
